status_reason: An exact configuration cannot be approved now because the contaminant and quality variable are undefined, and method selection requires knowing the analytical problem; for samples of incompletely known composition several methods must be tested first.
answer: No single method or exact sensor configuration can be recommended yet, because selecting a method requires knowing the analytical problem and for a liquid of incompletely known composition several optical methods must be tested first. The first step is a multi-method laboratory comparison (MIR ATR, NIR, Raman, fluorescence/UV-Vis) on retained in-spec and off-spec samples, followed by identifying key spectral features and only then choosing the method, probe and fiber. Before that, the client should supply the liquid composition, the off-spec quality variable, the measurement location and process conditions, and an independent laboratory reference.

inline.headline: Test MIR ATR first in the laboratory on in-spec versus off-spec liquid samples, compared with Raman and NIR, before choosing any in-line configuration.
inline.probe: MIR ATR fiber probe in contact with the liquid (ATR element material to be selected once the liquid is known, e.g. ZrO2 or diamond as used in AFS examples)
inline.install: unknown – ask (laboratory samples first; in-line point to be defined after the method is selected)
inline.not_final_because: The contaminant, quality variable, liquid composition, optical properties, location and process conditions are unknown, so MIR ATR is only the first method to screen alongside NIR, Raman and fluorescence, and the ATR probe sees only a very thin layer (usually <50 µm) of the liquid.

problems.text: An exact configuration is asked before the target is known, but choosing a method requires knowing the analytical problem and for samples of unknown composition several methods are tested first, so an immediate exact configuration would rest on invented facts.
The interface (ATR, transmission, transflection or reflection probe) depends on the method and the liquid's properties, which are not yet known, so probe type and path length cannot be fixed now.

Detecting a contaminant with broad-band methods (NIR, UV, fluorescence) needs chemometric models built and validated against independent references, so off-spec samples and a laboratory reference analysis are required before any decision.
NIR may lack sensitivity below 0.1 % and most chemicals do not fluoresce, so the contaminant level and nature decide which methods can see it at all.

methods.why: Mid-IR gives well-defined absorption peaks with high selectivity for liquids, which helps reveal an unknown chemical difference between in-spec and off-spec samples.
Raman probes liquids with high selectivity and carries information complementary to MIR, but fluorescence of organic compounds can mask its weak signal.
NIR is the most common online fiber-probe method with long silica cables, but its broad overlapping bands need chemometrics and it may lack sensitivity below 0.1 %.
Both are highly sensitive but have low selectivity and fluorescence only works if the contaminant or liquid contains fluorescing substances.

questions.q: What is the normal composition of the liquid and is it transparent, turbid or opaque?
questions.why: The liquid's composition and optical density decide the method and probe interface (ATR, transmission or reflection).

questions.q: Which quality variable goes off specification, and what candidate contaminants or sources do you suspect?
questions.why: Selecting a spectral method requires knowing the analytical problem.

questions.q: Can you provide retained in-spec and off-spec samples together with independent laboratory analyses of them?
questions.why: Several methods must be compared on real samples and chemometric models need independent reference values to be built and validated.

questions.q: Where would the probe be installed and what are the temperature, pressure, flow, cleaning and hazardous-area conditions there?
questions.why: Fiber probes allow remote in-line monitoring, but probe and fiber choice depend on the installation conditions.

questions.q: Do you need an alarm when the liquid deviates, or a quantitative value, and how fast must it respond?
questions.why: The task decides the method and technique and whether a classification or quantitative model is built.

technical.spectral_window: MIR ATR: mid-IR 4000–400 cm-1, of which PIR fiber transmits about 3–17 µm (approx. 3300–590 cm-1); Raman excitation and NIR window unknown – ask until screening
technical.probe: MIR ATR contact probe (ATR element material unknown – ask; ZrO2 or diamond tips are used in AFS examples); path length for transmission probes unknown – ask
technical.fiber: PIR fiber for MIR ATR; Vis-NIR silica for NIR/Raman; length and routing unknown – ask
technical.reference_method: unknown – ask (independent laboratory analysis of the off-spec quality variable)
technical.calibration: unknown – ask (retained in-spec and off-spec samples first; design after the target variable is known)

experiment.objective: Find out which optical method sees a spectral difference between retained in-spec and off-spec liquid samples, before selecting any in-line configuration.
steps: Collect retained in-spec and off-spec liquid samples and have them analysed by an independent laboratory reference method chosen by the client.
Measure all samples with the AFS multi-spectral fiber system using MIR ATR, Raman, NIR and fluorescence/UV-Vis probes.
Compare the spectra by multivariate analysis to identify which method and which spectral regions separate in-spec from off-spec samples.
Use the identified key spectral features to propose the method, probe interface, fiber and measurement point for a first in-line trial.
references: Independent laboratory analysis of each sample (method to be named by the client)
Client's own in-spec/off-spec classification of each sample
experiment.go_no_go: Criteria come from the client (required detection level and separation of off-spec samples).

pathway.key_features: Not yet known; to be identified by multivariate analysis of in-spec versus off-spec spectra.
pathway.path_reason: Path selection follows the multi-method lab test and key-feature selection, which have not been done.

multispectral.why: Raman carries information complementary to MIR, and combining heterogeneous information from two methods is the basis of the multispectral synergy effect.
multispectral.probe: Separate time-synchronised probes if the liquid is homogeneous at the measuring point; a combined multispectral probe if it is heterogeneous or changes rapidly.
multispectral.fusion: Low-level fusion of synchronised spectra with dedicated data-fusion algorithms, compared against a model per method.
multispectral.test: Build single-method and fused models on the same validation samples and accept the combination only if it beats the best single method.

assumptions: The process liquid can be sampled and retained in-spec and off-spec samples can be supplied for laboratory testing.
The contaminant is chemical in nature and may produce a spectral difference; this is unverified.
